texto: To highlight the subject **c'est** + subject + **qui**: **C'est Thomas qui a téléphoné** (it was Thomas who called) is used.
To highlight the object or time, **que**: **C'est hier que je suis rentré** is used (it was yesterday when I returned).
**Qui** goes with subject and **que** with the rest. It serves to change the order and give more strength to a part.

filas: C'est hier que je suis rentré.

analisis: It was Thomas who (emphasis on the subject)

frases.fr: C'est hier que je suis rentré.
frases.en: It was yesterday when I came back.

frases.fr: C'est précisément ce que je voulais dire.
frases.es: Es precisamente lo que quería decir.

frases.fr: Surtout, c'est important que tu viennes.
frases.es: Sobre todo, es importante que vengas.
frases.en: Above all, it's important that you come.

bloques.pregunta: How do you say «It was Thomas who called.»?

opciones.explicacion: «C'est» + subject + «qui».
With subject you should use «qui», not «que».
A form of present that does not translate the preterito.

bloques.pregunta: Which one is right for «It was yesterday when I got here.»?

opciones.texto: C'est hier que je suis arrivé.
opciones.explicacion: «C'est» + time circumstantial complement + «que».

opciones.texto: C'est hier qui je suis arrivé.
opciones.explicacion: «que», not «qui», is used with circumstantial supplements.

opciones.texto: C'est hier où je suis arrivé.
opciones.explicacion: «Où» is not used in the «c'est... que» relief fixed structure.
Relative title subject to the cleft structure.
It is used for direct object or circumstantial supplements.
It is reserved for regimens with the «de» preposition.
Relative title of direct object in the cleft structure.
It works as a subject of the verb, not as a direct object.
It is used with prepositional regimens with «de».
A categorical emphasis on the subject of action.
Present time that does not reflect the composite passé.
It misconverts emphatic affirmation into denial.

bloques.audio: C'est précisément ce que je voulais dire.

opciones.explicacion: «Précisément» emphasizes the exact concordance of ideas.
It turns prayer into a non-existent denial.
Alters verbal time from imperfect to present.

bloques.pregunta: How do you highlight a place complement like «That's where I work.»?

opciones.explicacion: «c'est... que» is used to highlight circumstantial additions of place or time.
The «qui» pronoun is only used when the element in relief is the subject.
In the standard emphatic construction with «c'est», the extraction relative is «que».

intro: Today we highlight the important: in French you can highlight a part of the phrase with «c'est... qui» or «c'est... que».
